findings.summary: Accepted manifests could omit runtime gate modules, use unsafe or symlinked paths, and crash exact hashing on non-UTF-8 Git blobs.
findings.resolution: Require every executable/imported gate module, canonical repository-relative non-symlink paths, lowercase SHA-256 values, commit ancestry, and byte-preserving git show hashing.

findings.summary: Dependency cycles with a later gate branch, dirty worktrees, and edit-then-revert gate history could pass.
findings.resolution: Propagate cycle blockers, reject meaningful dirty status, require first-work and gate ancestry, and scan every post-gate commit touching bound gate files.

findings.summary: An accepted manifest's review and owner hashes were syntactic strings rather than exact candidate/review/approval artifact bindings.
findings.resolution: Bind and revalidate non-consumable candidate bytes, zero-blocker review bytes, approval bytes, gate version, commit, and complete file map.

findings.summary: Indented task markers and plans with no completed tasks evaded completion, while generated revisions lacked ancestry validation and archive ambiguity was track-local.
findings.resolution: Parse task markers independent of indentation/bullet, require at least one completed task, require generated-fact ancestry, and reject any active/archive duplicate.

findings.summary: Git execution and supervisor Python import failures were not consistently structured and the inherited PYTHONPATH could influence the gate adapter.
findings.resolution: Convert Git OS/Unicode failures to blocked results and run the adapter with safe-path mode, repository-only PYTHONPATH, and bytecode writes disabled.

findings.summary: This fresh review session has no tool-attested OpenCode session export, spawn/event IDs, or fork_turns receipt.
findings.required_action: Obtain a raw OpenCode export/receipt for an independent fork_turns=none reviewer session, bind its exact hash and event IDs, then rerun review and regenerate the candidate/review binding.
